extracted.intended_audience: organizations seeking philanthropic grants from SFF, prospective applicants, and participating funders/donors
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions and procedural rules for the Survival and Flourishing Fund's grant-making programs (S-Process, Speculation Grants, Matching Pledges, Initiative Committee), how applications may be shared/processed, and how applicants can apply for specific funding types.

rubrics_metrics.name: The S-Process
rubrics_metrics.description: The S-Process is the algorithm and recurring meeting procedure we follow once or twice per year to produce grant recommendations to our participating Funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to run themed and main grant rounds (e.g. S-Process Grant Rounds, Main Round). S-Process recommendations are the primary mechanism by which SFF recommends grants to participating Funders; other programs (e.g. Speculation Grants) are related to or retroactively funded by S-Process recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculation Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculation Grants are an additional type of grant we make, using an experimental procedure for making decisions more quickly than the S-Process, that is retroactively funded by recommendations from the S-Process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are an alternative, faster decision-making mechanism; funding for Speculation Grants is validated/retroactively funded by subsequent S-Process recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching Pledges (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching Pledges are commitments made by Funders as part of an S-Process round to match outside donations to a recipient at some rate (e.g. 2-to-1), up to the pledged amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching Pledges are conditional on the grantee raising outside funds; in the grants table a '‡' symbol indicates a Matching Pledge awarded in addition to or instead of a standard S-Process recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The Initiative Committee is a small group, made up of Jaan Tallinn, SFF Advisors, and 2-5 anonymous voters, that makes grants on its own initiative, without receiving or requiring proposals or applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This committee can make grants outside of the S-Process application flow. The site notes that if you would like to propose a grant for SFF to make, the S-Process combined with Speculation Grants are probably still the most efficient route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessor independence and funder guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: SFF grant recommendations are made by a group of independent assessors whose membership changes regularly. The philanthropic priorities of SFF’s Funders play a guiding role (e.g. see Jaan Tallinn’s philanthropic priorities) but assessors are free to choose to support applications outside of these priority areas and will sometimes do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment is done by independent assessors (rotating membership). Funders' priorities guide but do not strictly determine assessor choices — applicants may be supported even if they are outside funders' stated priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application-sharing agreement with Effective Institutions Project (EIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: SFF is partnering with the Effective Institutions Project (EIP) to increase the funding pool available to SFF applicants by sharing applications to our SFF Funding Rolling Application with EIP. EIP anticipates recommending $5–15 million in grants to SFF applicants in 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to the SFF Funding Rolling Application should expect that their applications may be shared with EIP for consideration by that partner; this increases potential funding sources but also means applications may be considered by external partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching Pledge Program (application route)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting in 2025, SFF will be making some of its S-Process grant recommendations as Matching Pledges through the new Matching Pledge Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you would like to apply for a Matching Pledge, you can complete the Matching Pledge portion of the SFF Funding Rolling Application to be considered for the program. (Implied: applicants must use the specified portion of the rolling application to be eligible.)

rubrics_metrics.name: SFF as a virtual fund and grant processing channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Survival and Flourishing Fund is a 'virtual fund': we organize application submission and evaluation processes to help donors decide where to make donations. We maintain a DAF at the Silicon Valley Community Foundation under the same name (SFF), and we also occasionally process grant recommendations through other DAFs. Initiative Committee grants and occasionally other grants are processed through SFC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants recommended by SFF may be processed through different donor-advised funds or through Survival and Flourishing Corp (SFC); applicants and recipients should expect variability in processing channel and that SFF primarily coordinates evaluation and recommendation rather than directly holding all funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and labels of funding in recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant recommendations are described in the public list with labels such as 'General support', 'Conditional Support', 'Unconditional gift', and 'Pledged'. The '‡' symbol indicates a Matching Pledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These labels convey the nature of the recommended funding (e.g., general operating support vs conditional/pledged funds). Matching Pledges (‡) are conditional on outside fundraising; 'Pledged' entries indicate funds that are committed but may be processed later or require fulfillment conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcements and publication practice
rubrics_metrics.description: SFF posts Application Announcements, Recommendations, and Further Funding Opportunities for each round. The site notes that recommendations after the final date might not be listed yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should monitor announcements for application windows and outcomes; published totals sometimes exceed initial estimates and some rounds close after announcement. The site provides public transparency about rounds, amounts, and recipients.
